title: Review Team Standards: Waiver of a Host Cancellation Penalty
content:
# Review Team Standards — Waiver of a Host Cancellation Penalty (Host Accounts)

## Standard

A host who cancelled for a documented reason — an extenuating circumstance, a guest's breach of house rules, a major disruptive event, or a safety concern — appeals the penalty through a cancellation penalty appeal naming the penalty charge as its related event.

A penalty is waived only when the penalty appeal has been approved.

The penalty appeal must have been submitted within the penalty appeal period of the account's tier (14 calendar days after the host cancellation); the days are counted from the date of the cancellation to the date part of the appeal's submission time, and an appeal on the last day stands.

## Effect of an approved waiver

- The waiver gives back the whole penalty charged, never part of it.
- It is booked once per cancelled stay.
- The waived cancellation is no longer counted in the host's cancellation rate.
- The calendar block on the cancelled nights stays.

## Conditions in combination

| Penalty appeal approved | Submitted within the 14 days | Waiver |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Both conditions of this standard hold |
| Yes | No | Not waived — the appeal was not submitted within the period |
| No (still submitted and undecided, or denied) | Yes or no | Not waived — the appeal has not been approved |

## Boundary of the appeal period (hypothetical dates)

Host cancellation dated 2 March:

| Appeal submitted at | Days counted | Within the period? |
|---|---|---|
| 16 March, 23:40 | 14 | Yes — the last day stands |
| 17 March, 00:05 | 15 | No |

The time of day does not count; only the date part of the submission is compared.

## Questions

**Can part of a penalty be waived?** No. An approved waiver gives back the whole penalty charged.

**Does a waiver lift the calendar block on the cancelled nights?** No. The block stays.
